note: Criterion names, mark ranges and band boundaries are factual features of the assessment model. All descriptor wording below is EconIB's own plain-English rendering, written to be diagnostic. It is not IB text. Always check the official subject guide and your teacher's marking.
model: Each rubric is a set of dimensions. Every dimension has the same five-rung ladder (0-4). Your band is set by your weakest dimensions, not your best — which is why the fix is always the lowest rung, never more of what you already do well.

ia.name: Internal assessment portfolio
ia.structure: Each of the three commentaries is marked out of 14 on criteria A-E. Criterion F is applied once to the whole portfolio, out of 3. 14 x 3 + 3 = 45.

criteria.name: Diagrams
criteria.assesses: Whether you can construct a diagram and explain it.

levels.text: No relevant diagram, or nothing that meets the description below.
A relevant diagram is there, but it is not explained — or the explanation is wrong.
The diagram is relevant, accurate and correctly labelled, but the explanation is thin.
The diagram is relevant, accurate and correctly labelled, and it is fully explained in the text.

criteria.howToMove: Most students sit on 2. The gap to 3 is almost never the drawing — it is that the prose never walks the reader through the shift. Name the curve, say why it moved, and state what happened to price and quantity, referring to your own labels.

criteria.name: Terminology
criteria.assesses: Whether you use economic terminology appropriately.

levels.text: No relevant economic terminology, or nothing that meets the description below.
Economic terminology relevant to the article appears in the commentary.
Relevant economic terminology is used correctly throughout, not just in one patch.

criteria.howToMove: Throughout is the operative word. Terms clustered in an opening definitions paragraph and then abandoned reads as 1. Use precise terms where the analysis happens.

criteria.name: Application and analysis
criteria.assesses: Whether you apply economic theory to this article and analyse with it.

levels.text: No relevant theory applied, or nothing that meets the description below.
Relevant theory is applied to the article, but the analysis is limited.
Relevant theory is applied throughout, with sound economic analysis.
Relevant theory is applied throughout, with effective economic analysis.

criteria.howToMove: The difference between 2 and 3 is causal chains that reach an outcome. Not 'a tax reduces demand' but 'the tax raises unit cost, shifting supply left, raising price to P2 and cutting quantity to Q2, with the burden split by relative elasticities'.

criteria.name: Key concept
criteria.assesses: Whether you link one of the nine key concepts to the article.

levels.text: No key concept identified — or the key concept has already been used in another commentary in this portfolio.
A key concept is named and there is an attempt to link it to the article.
A key concept is named and the link to the article is partly explained.
A key concept is named and the link to the article is fully explained.

criteria.howToMove: The cheapest lost marks in the whole IA. Reusing a concept across two commentaries scores 0 here, and across three costs you up to 6 marks. Pick your three concepts before you write anything, and make the concept the lens of the analysis rather than a sentence bolted to the end.

criteria.name: Evaluation
criteria.assesses: Whether your judgments are supported by reasoned argument.

levels.text: No judgments, or nothing that meets the description below.
Judgments are made but the reasoning behind them is limited.
Judgments are made and supported by appropriate reasoning.
Judgments are made and supported by effective and balanced reasoning.

criteria.howToMove: Balanced is the word that decides 3. Give the strongest version of the other side, then say what your judgment depends on — magnitude, time frame, elasticity, or who bears the cost.

criteria.name: Rubric requirements
criteria.assesses: Three portfolio-level requirements. One mark each.

requirements.text: Each article is based on a different unit of the syllabus (Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, The global economy — Unit 1 is excluded).
Each article comes from a different and appropriate source.
Each article was published no earlier than one year before that commentary was written.

levels.text: No requirement met.
One requirement met.
Two requirements met.
All three requirements met.

criteria.howToMove: These three marks are free and are decided by admin, not economics. EconIB checks them for you deterministically — no judgment involved.
